answer: Lagoon-bound echo anchoring. Each agent periodically broadcasts a unique signed “echo” derived from its private key and a shared comet-seeded randomness beacon; peers record the echo in a local lagoon shard. New agents must collect N distinct historical echoes from existing agents before transacting. Cloning requires replicating N independent timelines, costing N× storage and bandwidth per identity, while honest agents pay only one periodic broadcast.
